subject: Urgent: Embeddings p95/p99 Latency Surge after Catalog Sync - DataCorp Impacting Search
messages:
From: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@datacorp.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: support@datacorp.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 18:08:00 -0500
Subject: Search embeddings suddenly slow this morning

Hi Neha,

We've been seeing search slowdowns starting ~09:00 PST this morning. p95 and p99 for embeddings-based nearest neighbor calls jumped from ~60ms up to 900ms and some requests are timing out at 3s. This is causing a ~15% failure rate for our realtime search bar and a lot of customer complaints.

We haven't changed our integration. Anything on Redwood's side we should be aware of? Our internal SRE suspects a model change but we don't have visibility into catalog sync timing. Can you confirm what changed and ETA to restore latency?

Attached: small sample of failed request IDs and timestamps (incidents/snapshot-20261129-15.csv).

Thanks,
Lydia
Lydia Chen

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, oncall-embeds@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Search embeddings suddenly slow this morning

Oncall note: 09:00 PST coincides with a catalog sync that deployed two new embedding variants (quantized-8 and q4f32 fallback config) to hosted pool A. Initial telemetry: small increase in cold-start KV cache misses and larger average KV sizes for the new variants. We're seeing batching behavior shift: more small batches at higher concurrency due to slight change in tokenization (model input headers).

Mitigations performed (in order):
1) Increased target batch window on pool A to reduce small-batch penalty (partial effect).
2) Forced fallback to previous variant for customer groups served from pool A (rolled out at 16:15 PST).
3) Reenabled prefix caching for sessions that were impacted after discovering an evict-on-sync regression.

Initial result: p95 improved from ~900ms -> ~220ms within 30m after fallbacks, p99 persisted ~600ms for some long-tail requests. Continuing to monitor.

Attaching heap trace snapshot and a short log extract (heap-trace-embed-20261129.txt).

—Marcus
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@datacorp.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Search embeddings suddenly slow this morning

Hi Lydia — thanks for flagging and for the sample. We're actively working on this and we've applied a rollback/fallback for the hosts serving your traffic.

What we have so far:
- Root cause appears to be a catalog sync that exposed a variant with a slightly different tokenization path, which increased KV cache churn and shifted effective batching.
- We've pinned DataCorp's traffic to the previous embedding variant and re-enabled prefix caching for your sessions.

Short ETA: we expect most degraded requests to recover within the next 45–60 minutes. I'll update you by 17:30 PST or earlier if we see full recovery.

If you can, please share any additional failed request IDs and confirm whether timeouts are still occurring after 17:30 PST.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Escalation: Exec brief request — embeddings tail latency for DataCorp

Heads up — DataCorp's search SLOs were hit and exec attention is requested. I'm preparing a short briefing for leadership with: impact window, customers affected list, mitigation timeline, and recommended longer-term actions (catalog rollout gating, canary traffic split, and a safeguards checklist).

Quick numbers to include:
- Impact window: 09:00–16:15 PST (catalog sync at 09:02; fallback at 16:15)
- Peak p95/p99 observed: 900ms / 2.8s
- Post-mitigation p95/p99 (rolling): 220ms / ~600ms
- Affected % of DataCorp requests: ~18% error/timeout spike, 55% elevated latency for a 2-hour tail window

Attaching internal incident link and the support artifact: https://app.redwood.io/incidents/INC-20261129-embed-latency

Recommend we loop in Product Ops to add a catalog rollout policy: require canary with prefix-cache validation and a degradation detector (configs that change tokenization path). Laura, can you review the recommended wording for the leadership note?

—Rishi
Technical Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@datacorp.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: support@datacorp.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Search embeddings suddenly slow this morning

Thanks — Monica and team. After the pinning we saw most requests drop back to expected latency. Our SRE ran a short backfill of traffic and confirmed the search bar p99 is within normal bounds now.

Concerns from us: we need advance notice on catalog variant changes (especially quantization/tokenization changes) and a plan for preserving prefix cache across syncs. We're open to a monthly sync window or canary policy.

Appreciate the fast response. Please keep us looped on the postmortem and any rollout policy changes.

—Lydia
Platform Engineering, DataCorp
